records.name: S2_cross_check_vs_eq2p3
records.detail: F228/eq2.3 ratio at M_form=(10000.0, 1000000.0, 100000000.0) g: [11.7165, 11.7165, 11.7165] (constant to 3.03e-16 relative spread). NOTE (review-finding attack 2): the constant ratio is EXPECTED, not a discovery -- both formulas share the same M^1.5 scaling by construction (entropy-conserved comoving relic number), so any two such formulas give an exactly-constant ratio regardless of whether their O(1) normalisations agree. The only informative content is that mean ratio 11.716 -- i.e. the two independently-chosen O(1) normalisations (F228's gamma_coll/g_star convention vs eq2.3's) differ by only ~12x, unremarkable at F228's own declared order-of-magnitude tier. This is a mild, not a strong, cross-check.

records.name: S3_formation_mass_ceiling
records.detail: DLS crossover M_form=1.609e+08 g; PVL crossover M_form=1.680e+11 g -- DLS is the tighter bound across this range, consistent with 2506.16154's own statement that DLS dominates PVL for M_form below ~1e9 g. Order-of-magnitude ceiling: M_form <~ 1.6e+08 g. CAVEAT (review-finding attack 6): 2506.16154 itself states the DLS bound assumes a MONOCHROMATIC PBH mass function that 'may not reflect a realistic physical scenario,' and that early PBH mergers may weaken it -- so this is an order-of-magnitude placement against a bound that is itself model-dependent, not an unconditional exclusion.

records.name: S6_gaussianity_requirement
records.detail: P_R at M_form=(10000.0, 1000000.0, 100000000.0) g -- general-integral convention (Eq.9, P_R=(81/16)sigma^2): [0.0173, 0.0224, 0.0317] (3/3 inside the stated band); THIS PAPER'S OWN narrow-bump convention (Eq.10, P_R=(9/4)sigma^2 -- what it uses for its own headline number): [0.0077, 0.01, 0.0141] (1/3 inside the stated band). The two conventions disagree on which side of the arXiv:2509.20533 P_R~[0.01,0.1] LIGO-O3-Gaussian-exclusion band edge the result falls (review-finding attack 6, 2026-09-04) -- so this is graded on 'same order of magnitude as the excluded band' (bracketed), not 'inside the band' (quantitative). EXACTNESS: bracketed. Also (attack 5): because sigma_req=erfc^-1 compresses ~20 orders of magnitude in beta into O(1) range in sigma, landing near this band is not a sharp coincidence -- most sub-dominant beta values would land somewhere in a similar range. This is reported as a same-regime PLAUSIBILITY argument, not a from-first-principles exclusion (see Sec.5-6 of F365 and its Reviewed & corrected note).
